title: datasette-llm 0.1a11
summary:
Release: datasette-llm 0.1a11 

 datasette-llm is the intermediate plugin for Datasette that supports configuring LLMs for use with other Datasette plugins.

 This release adds support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so you can configure Datasette to use an LLM hosted anywhere that talks the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol.

 This means that if you're running local models with LM Studio or Ollama or llama.cpp (which just hit v1.0.0 ) you can run Datasette via uvx like this:

 wget https://datasette.io/content.db

uvx --with datasette-agent datasette \
 --root --secret 1 \
 -s plugins.datasette-llm.default_model ' { 
 "model": "lmstudio-qwen", 
 "model_name": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b", 
 "api_base": "http://localhost:1234/v1" 
 } ' content.db 

 And you'll get a local server running a Datasette Agent instance powered by your local model!

 Tags: uv , datasette-agent , llm , datasette , llms , ai , generative-ai

title: datasette-vega 0.7
summary:
Release: datasette-vega 0.7 

 A new release of Datasette's longest untouched plugin, for rendering charts (using Vega-Lite ) against data in a table or custom query. The last release was in July 2018!

 I finally bumped it for compatibility with the latest Datasette alphas, plus some cosmetic tweaks to make it work better with Datasette Lite .

 (Datasette Lite just gained the ability to run JavaScript plugins like this! I'll write more about that soon.)

 Since it works with Datasette Lite, the live demo in the README now links to this demo on Datasette Lite .

 Tags: datasette , visualisation , datasette-lite

title: Open-source AI without Jensen
summary:
The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a major setback for the US development of an open model ecosystem. Nvidia still has the financial interests in supporting open models, which are to avoid concentration in power among a few customers who would develop their own chips and reduce Nvidia’s profits, but supporting the open ecosystem is a tricky puzzle more than an engineering problem to grind out a solution on.
 Nvidia’s business operations are famously extremely dependent on Jensen as an operator, so it is a consensus opinion that there are challenges ahead (or even more high-profile departures through chip-smuggling investigations or plain-old sharks circling more poachable talent). Nvidia’s number one goal is to stabilize the ship, deliver to customers in the next 24 months, and prevent implosion. Open models have been one of Jensen’s more ambitious, founder-style bets. He has been flooding the zone with funding in a way that will very likely dry up.

title: Import AI 480: Self-sustaining space economies; AI for science progress, and Meta builds perfect hands for a superintelligence
summary:
Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe.
 Subscribe now 
 AI Science startup converts a quantum conjecture into a theorem:
 …An evocative taste of the singularity…
 In the same way a few years ago it went from remarkable to unremarkable to see computers gain the ability to identify objects in images, we’re now in an era where it’s rapidly going from remarkable to unremarkable for computers to extend the bounds of human knowledge.
 The latest example comes from Physical Superintelligence, an AI science startup which has proved a longstanding quantum computing conjecture.

 What they did: “Open since 2008, the conjecture of Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis concerns when quantum computers can be exponentially faster than ordinary ones. Now, a research system developed internally at Physical Superintelligence (PSI), running a non-public Anthropic model, found a proof for it, settling one of the most fundamental questions in quantum computing,” the startup writes. “The system had a complete proof of the conjecture during the third day of the run, and Lean, a proof assistant in which a computer checks every step, accepted it. We then set the system to work on related open problems. Along the way, the system improved the result twice, and Lean accepted the final version.”
